correctness.rationale: For fixed 0<alpha<1, h>0 and 0<delta<=(1-sqrt(alpha))^2, derive exact second-order scalar recurrence from the branch matrices with x_-1=0 and q=mu/alpha. Distinct roots yield a positive dominant contracting mode and crossing index L/|log lambda|+O(1). At delta=(1-sqrt(alpha))^2, direct Jordan solution has Jordan linear-in-iterate prefactor times geometric decay and gives (L+log L)/|log t|+O(1). At first crossing, consecutive negative and nonnegative positions are both O(q), after which the right branch increases strictly and its growing multiplier gamma>1 gives L/log gamma+O(1). Eight exact Fraction orbits and 8 bounded-remainder diagnostics passed from CHECKER.py; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: The natural nonsmooth-fold escape problem has a qualitative no-recurrence theorem but no sharp residence time. Along an open region of positive stable branch multipliers the passage is logarithmic; at the intrinsic, analytically determined critical-damping/Jordan boundary, the same physical passage time acquires an explicit, strictly positive log-log correction with bounded error. This resolves a meaningful spectral boundary and gives quantitative tipping clocks rather than an arbitrary finite parameter tabulation. No broader nonlinear theorem is claimed.
